Healthy.title: Healthy Leaf Condition
Healthy.description: The leaf shows optimal chlorophyll concentration, vibrant green pigmentation, and healthy vascular structure with no significant visual signs of nutrient or vitamin deficiencies.
symptoms: Uniform green leaf lamina
Intact leaf margins with no scorching
Smooth texture without mottling or chlorosis
organic_remedies: Maintain regular balanced organic watering schedule
Apply well-aged compost or vermicompost every 4-6 weeks
Ensure adequate sunlight exposure and well-draining soil
Healthy.preventive_care: Periodically test soil pH (6.0 - 7.0 optimal for most medicinal plants) and mulch to preserve soil moisture.

Nitrogen (N).title: Nitrogen / Protein Deficiency
Nitrogen (N).description: Nitrogen is essential for chlorophyll synthesis, protein formation, and vegetative growth. Deficiency causes uniform chlorosis (yellowing) starting on older leaves as nitrogen is mobile.
symptoms: General pale green to yellowing across older lower leaves
Stunted plant growth and thinner stems
Early leaf drop in severe cases
organic_remedies: Apply Nitrogen-rich organic liquid fertilizers like Neem cake solution or Fish hydrolysate
Top-dress soil with well-rotted cow manure or vermicompost
Foliar spray with diluted seaweed extract (Kelp meal)
Nitrogen (N).preventive_care: Incorporate nitrogen-fixing cover crops (pulse crops/legumes) in soil rotation.

Phosphorus (P).title: Phosphorus / ATP Energy Deficiency
Phosphorus (P).description: Phosphorus plays a crucial role in energy transfer (ATP), nucleic acid synthesis, root development, and flowering. Lack of phosphorus leads to anthocyanin accumulation, causing purpling or dark bronze leaves.
symptoms: Reddish-purple or dark bronze discoloration on leaf undersides and margins
Delayed leaf emergence and poor root growth
Dull dark green foliage with delayed maturation
organic_remedies: Apply organic Bone Meal or Rock Phosphate to root zone
Incorporate composted poultry manure or wood ash into topsoil
Apply Mycorrhizal fungi inoculants to enhance phosphorus uptake
Phosphorus (P).preventive_care: Maintain soil pH between 6.2 and 7.0, as acidic or alkaline extremes bind phosphorus.

Potassium (K).title: Potassium / Osmotic Balance Deficiency
Potassium (K).description: Potassium regulates stomatal opening, water uptake, enzyme activation, and disease resistance. Deficiency causes marginal necrosis (scorching along leaf edges) and curling.
symptoms: Browning, scorching, and drying along leaf edges (marginal scorch)
Yellowing (chlorosis) progressing inward from leaf margins
Weak stems and high susceptibility to drought or pest stress
organic_remedies: Apply Potassium-rich Wood Ash or Kelp meal tea
Incorporate Banana peel tea or Greensand into soil mix
Drench soil with Potassium sulfate (organic certified)
Potassium (K).preventive_care: Ensure adequate soil organic matter to prevent potassium leaching in sandy soils.

Magnesium (Mg).title: Magnesium / Chlorophyll Core Deficiency
Magnesium (Mg).description: Magnesium is the central atom of the chlorophyll molecule and acts as an enzyme activator. Deficiency results in classic interveinal chlorosis on mature leaves while veins remain green.
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis (yellowing between dark green veins) on mature foliage
Brittle, curled leaf edges in advanced stages
Reddish or pale yellow patches between leaf veins
organic_remedies: Apply Epsom Salt (Magnesium Sulfate) foliar spray: 1 tbsp per gallon of water
Drench soil with Dolomitic limestone (if soil pH is acidic)
Apply composted leaves and hardwood ash
Magnesium (Mg).preventive_care: Avoid excessive potassium or calcium fertilization which can block magnesium absorption.

Iron (Fe).title: Iron / Enzymatic Chlorosis Deficiency
Iron (Fe).description: Iron is required for electron transport, chlorophyll biosynthesis, and respiratory enzymes. Because iron is immobile, deficiency causes striking interveinal chlorosis on young emerging leaves.
symptoms: Severe yellowing to near white interveinal chlorosis on young leaves
Vascular network (veins) remains sharply dark green
Stunted shoot tip development
organic_remedies: Apply Chelated Iron (Fe-EDDHA or Fe-DTPA) as a foliar spray or soil drench
Foliar spray with organic liquid iron kelp complex
Add elemental sulfur or acidic compost if high soil pH is immobilizing iron
Iron (Fe).preventive_care: Prevent over-watering and soil compaction which reduces root oxygenation and iron uptake.

Calcium (Ca).title: Calcium / Cell Wall Structure Deficiency
Calcium (Ca).description: Calcium is a structural component of plant cell walls and cell membranes. Immobile in plant tissues, deficiency manifests as distorted young leaves, tip burn, and localized tissue necrosis.
symptoms: Hooked or distorted young growing leaf tips
Necrotic brown spots and tip burn on new growth
Weak plant structure and blossom end rot in fruiting medicinal plants
organic_remedies: Apply crushed eggshell tea or Gypsum (Calcium Sulfate)
Foliar spray with liquid calcium chloride solution
Incorporate Agricultural Lime or Bone Meal into root zone
Calcium (Ca).preventive_care: Maintain steady, uniform irrigation schedules; fluctuating water levels disrupt calcium transport.

Zinc (Zn).title: Zinc / Auxin Enzyme Deficiency
Zinc (Zn).description: Zinc is essential for plant growth hormone (auxin) production, internode elongation, and protein metabolism. Deficiency results in mottled chlorosis, leaf bronzing, and shortened internodes.
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis with light green/yellow mottled spots
Shortened internodes resulting in a 'rosette' appearance
Small, distorted leaf growth ('little leaf')
organic_remedies: Apply Zinc Sulfate foliar spray (0.5% solution)
Apply organic zinc-chelate compound to soil
Incorporate zinc-enriched composted organic matter
Zinc (Zn).preventive_care: Avoid excessive phosphorus fertilizer application which precipitates zinc in soil.
